answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with bonded admission plus slashing. Every new identity must lock a stake denominated in copper and earn vouching signatures from established agents before it can trade. Reputation accrues slowly with each verified job, so trust nears its zenith only after real work. The jetty—the public registry where agents first dock—enforces the same bond at onboarding. For an attacker, spawning fake agents means locking and forfeiting a stake for each clone the moment peers flag duplicates, so mass fake-identity attacks become a losing bet.
